policy: Free models first, then medium-cost. Nothing above the price cap: costly work stays on Claude (Opus) via the subscription.
evidence: Chosen 2026-09-15 from the live OpenRouter catalogue, a 3-task probe (bug finding, JSON extraction, length-constrained summary; a reliability filter, not a quality ranking), a data_collection=deny + price-cap check per model, and public benchmarks (mostly vendor-reported).

code_review.use_for: First-pass review of large files or diffs for bugs, edge cases and security issues. Claude verifies every finding.
code_review.notes: North Mini Code was concise and complete in the probe. Use Kimi K2.7 Code (coding specialist, vendor-only benchmarks) only when the cheaper reviews look shallow.

summarise_extract.use_for: Summarising or extracting structured data from long files, logs, audit reports or JSON, returning short output.
summarise_extract.notes: GLM-5.3 Flash: cheapest full-score model, terse, 1.3M context. Dots-3 has 512K context but is wordy, so ask for bullets or JSON.

draft_code.use_for: Drafting boilerplate, tests, scripts, regexes or small functions that Claude then checks with check/build/tests.
draft_code.notes: GPT-5.6 Luna was fast and terse and leads cheap models on public coding comparisons. Qwen3 Coder Next is fastest but missed a bug in the review probe, so use it for drafting, not review.

debug_second_opinion.use_for: A bug Claude is stuck on after one real attempt: root-cause hypotheses from a different model family.
debug_second_opinion.notes: The one task where reasoning is worth paying for. DeepSeek V4 Pro is the strongest reasoner under the cap (vendor-reported). Include the error, relevant files via file_paths, and what Claude already ruled out.

compare_perspectives.use_for: Design trade-offs or ambiguous questions where disagreement between model families is itself useful.
compare_perspectives.notes: Pass either the two free models or the three medium ones (three vendors). Claude synthesises and decides.

quick_question.use_for: Short technical questions (API usage, library behaviour, explaining an error message) that don't need repo context.
quick_question.notes: Only worth it when the answer would otherwise cost Claude a long investigation. Check answers against docs or code.

keep_on_claude: High-risk code: AtlasMap/Timeline core, validator, build config
Multi-file edits that need repo context
Final review before reporting work done
Historical research, sourcing and fact-checking (an external model is never a source)
Anything that would need a model above the price cap: use Opus on the subscription
Small tasks, where the handoff costs more than it saves
